title: Continuous self-review
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing a repository, site or video on a rotation, run after run: scopes with the checks each needs from other packs, a schedule that stays a proposal until a person approves it, the next scopes picked by a fixed rule from what was reviewed least recently or changed most, each run's findings diffed against the last run into new, still open, fixed, unverified, unexplained, unchecked and reopened, fixes verified by a different worker, a review log that shows coverage over time, and a self-review before any change is handed on.
boundaries: A schedule is a proposal until a person approves it; this pack activates no scheduler and enqueues nothing.
The checks belong to their own packs and run as their own verbs; this pack picks, diffs and logs.
The review log is append-only, updated by compare-and-set; no entry is edited or removed.
A worker never verifies its own fix or approves its own change.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for reviewing a repository, site or video on a rotation, run after run

value.lets_workers: Cut a repository, site or video into scopes with the checks each needs from other packs; propose a review schedule that waits for a person's approval; pick the next scopes by a fixed rule from what was reviewed least recently or changed most; diff each run's findings against the last run of the same scope, so new, still open, fixed, unverified, unexplained, unchecked and reopened findings are told apart; propose the fix, verification and reproduction each one needs, with a different worker verifying; keep a review log that shows coverage over time; and review one's own change before handing it on.

flow.when: Once per target, and again when its structure changes.
A person approves the schedule, with an expiry; until then nothing runs on it.
Each approved window, or by hand.
After the picked scope's checks report.
A different worker verifies every fix the diff finds unverified.
Before a worker hands any change on.

complements: The checks themselves belong to other packs, such as codebase health review, edge and corner cases, accessibility audit, screenshot design review, video QA, annoyance hunt and wiring and conformance checks; this pack decides which scope runs when and what changed since last time.
Findings, fixes, independent verification and guards come from the findings to fixes pack; a cause that keeps coming back goes to its review-patterns.
The person's approval reuses the unattended run record pack's run approval, and an unattended window follows its run guards.
Comparing measured numbers with an accepted baseline is the regression watch pack; this pack compares findings with the last run.

nouns.title: How a repository, site or video is reviewed on a rotation, run after run
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: map-scopes cuts the target into scopes, names each scope's checks from other packs, and proposes a review schedule.
approve-schedule is a person's verb: until it is recorded, the schedule is only a proposal and nothing runs on it.
pick-scope applies the rotation rule to the review log and proposes the picked scopes' checks, at most ten verbs per pick.
The checks run as their own packs' verbs, each with its own receipt.

diff-against-last-run compares this run's findings with the last run of the same scope and sorts each into new, still open, fixed, gone without verification, gone unexplained, not checked or reopened.
log-run appends the run to the review log by compare-and-set, so coverage over time stays visible.
review-coverage reads the log across a window for scopes left out, checks that never fail or never run, and causes that keep coming back.
review-own-change is the self-review a worker runs on its own change before handing it to a different worker.
rules: A schedule is a proposal until a person approves it, with scopes, an allowance and an expiry.
Gone is not fixed: a finding is fixed only when a fix is recorded and a worker other than the fixer verified it.
A check that did not run is not a pass; the findings it would have seen stay open as not checked.
Diff only like with like: the same scope and the same check versions as the last run.
A finding seen again after it was closed is reopened, and its guard failed to catch it, so a stronger guard is proposed.
Self-review comes first and is never the last word: the worker that made a change never approves or verifies it.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a review schedule is a proposal until a person approves it
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A review schedule is a proposal until a person approves it. The approval names the scopes, the cadence, the allowance per window and an expiry; nothing runs on a schedule whose approval is missing or expired, and changing the schedule needs a new approval.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every scheduled run names an approval that covers its scope and has not expired; a run without one says manual and names who asked for it.

nouns.title: Guardrail: a finding that is not seen again is not yet fixed
nouns.category_reason: A guardrail is a reusable rule every verb in this work follows, with the check that proves it.

value.rule: A finding that the last run saw and this run did not is fixed only when a fix is recorded and a worker other than the fixer verified it. Without a fix it is gone unexplained and is reproduced; with an unverified fix it waits for verification; if its check did not run, it stays open.
value.how_it_is_checked: Every fixed row in a diff names its fix and a verification by a different worker or a person.

nouns.title: Picking the next scopes: least recently reviewed or changed most
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same log, catalog and churn always pick the same scopes.

order: Scopes never reviewed come first, in catalog order.
Urgent scopes come next: those more than twice their max interval since their last review, most overdue first by days over interval.

Every other scope gets score = days since its last review / its max interval + min(churn since then / its churn cap, 1) + 0.5 x min(open P0 and P1 findings, 2), rounded to three places, highest first.
Ties go to the lower scope id.
value.pick: Take the first scopes_per_window scopes the approved schedule allows.
value.overdue: A scope is overdue when its days since review exceed its max interval, and urgent when they exceed twice it.
value.no_starving: However busy other scopes are, a scope becomes urgent once it is twice its interval past its last review, and urgent scopes go before every other scope that has been reviewed. When a window's slots cover the scopes that come due, every scope is reviewed within about twice its interval; when they do not, the coverage review shows it and a person widens the window.
value.churn: Changed lines under a repository path, changed page digests for a site page, or changed renders for a video segment, since the last review.

nouns.title: Sorting this run's findings against the last run's
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same two runs always sort the same way.

value.match_by: The findings to fixes fingerprint, so a finding keeps its identity across runs.

seen_now.still_open: Seen by the last run and again now, with no verified fix.
seen_now.reopened: Closed as resolved before, or open with a fix a different worker verified, and seen again now: the fix did not hold and its guard missed it.
seen_now.decided: Closed before by a person's decision, as won't fix or duplicate, and seen again: listed under decided_seen with that decision, never reopened or proposed for a fix.

not_seen_now.not_checked: Its check did not run this time, or the check's version changed since the last run; it stays open.
not_seen_now.fixed: A fix is recorded and a worker other than the fixer verified it.
not_seen_now.gone_unverified: A fix is recorded but not yet verified by another worker.
not_seen_now.gone_unexplained: No fix is recorded; it may be hidden, moved or intermittent.

value.first_run: The first run of a scope, and only that run, carries nothing from a previous run: every finding is new.

nouns.title: Cutting a repository, site or video into scopes, and the checks each kind needs
nouns.category_reason: A reusable description of how to scope a review and which packs' checks to run.

kinds.cut: A folder or package that one worker can review in one sitting.
A stretch of a cut between two scene changes, or the whole cut when it is short.

value.baseline_checks: Any scope can also add regression-watch.compare-to-baseline when it has an accepted baseline.
value.rule: Give each scope a max interval: 14 days for code and pages people use every day, 30 for documentation and videos.

nouns.title: Reviewing your own change before anyone else does
nouns.category_reason: A zero-call rule set for self-review.

steps: Map the change's paths to the scopes they touch in the catalog.
Run those scopes' deterministic checks on the change, and list any that cannot run.
Record every problem found in your own work at once as a finding, even one you will fix in the next minute.
Hand the change and the self-review to a different worker or a person; never approve it yourself.
never: Mark your own change verified or approved.
Leave a problem you found off the record because you fixed it.

nouns.title: Record checks for review runs, with synthetic golden runs
nouns.category_reason: Deterministic checks with synthetic known-good and known-bad records; the validator recomputes every verdict.

value.purpose: Checks every review run must pass before it is appended to the log: the pinned scope and exact version, a person's approval for a scheduled run or a named requester for a manual one, the run it is compared with, checks that ran with their outputs and checks that did not with reasons, and every finding sorted with its follow-up: new ones recorded, fixed ones verified by someone other than the fixer, unverified and unexplained ones given a verification or a reproduction, unchecked ones kept open and reopened ones naming the closing they undid. The two synthetic good runs pass; each synthetic bad one fails exactly the one check named in fails.

deterministic_checks.why: The run pins the exact scope it reviewed.
The run names the exact version it reviewed.
A scheduled run names the person's approval it ran under.
A manual run names who asked for it.
A run that is not the first names the run it is compared with.
A first run carries nothing from a previous run, so it cannot hide findings by calling itself first.
Every check that ran gives its result and the digest of its output, so a claimed run traces to what it produced.
A check marked not run, skipped or unknown is listed under checks_not_run, never among the checks that ran.
Every check that did not run says why.
A finding is fixed only with a fix, a verification and who verified it.
The worker that made a fix never verifies it.
A fix nobody verified yet carries its proposed verb, verify-fix by the diff rules; diff-against-last-run's acceptance recomputes which.
A finding gone with no fix carries its proposed verb, reproduce by the diff rules.
A finding whose check did not run stays open, naming the check.
A reopened finding names the closing or verification it undid and its next verb, triage by the diff rules.

verbs.title: Cut the target into scopes and propose a schedule
verbs.summary: Cut a repository, site or video into scopes one worker can review in one sitting, give each its checks from other packs, a max interval and a churn measure, and write a review schedule proposal that waits for a person.
verbs.outcome: A scope catalog and a schedule proposal.

slots.name: target_brief
slots.description: Pin of a brief naming the target, its owner and the budget a review may use.

steps: Read the target: the repository tree at a commit, the site's page list or the video's scene changes.
Cut it into scopes by the scope kinds, give each scope the checks its kind needs, and a max interval.
Propose a cadence, scopes per window and an allowance per window that fit the requester's stated budget.
Leave activation not_activated and start and stop empty; only a person's approval sets them.

acceptance.check: The catalog validates against template.scope-catalog's schema.
The schedule validates against template.review-schedule's schema.
Every check names a verb template in this library.
Each scope is small enough for one review run.

network: Read-only page loads of the target site's own pages to list them; repositories and videos are read from a local copy.

verbs.title: Approve the review schedule (a person)
verbs.summary: The person who owns the target reads the schedule proposal and approves it, approves it with changes or declines it, with the scopes, the allowance and an expiry. This template performs nothing itself.

slots.name: review_schedule
slots.description: Pin of the review schedule proposal.

steps: Read the scopes, cadence, allowance per window and the checks each scope would run.
Approve only what you would accept running every window until the expiry; set the expiry.

acceptance.check: The approval validates against template.run-approval's schema.
expires is filled.

verbs.title: Pick the next scopes by the rotation rule
verbs.summary: Apply the rotation rule to the scope catalog and the review log as of now, rank every scope, pick the window's scopes, and propose their checks.
verbs.outcome: A scope pick, with the picked scopes' checks proposed.

slots.name: approval
slots.description: Pin of the person's schedule approval; leave empty only for a manual pick.

steps: Confirm an approval covers this window and has not expired, unless the requester asked for a manual pick; otherwise end blocked.
Measure each scope's churn since its last review and count its open P0 and P1 findings.
Rank by the rotation rule and pick the first scopes the approval allows.
Propose each picked scope's checks with the target version pinned, at most ten verbs; never enqueue them.

acceptance.check: The pick validates against template.scope-pick's schema.
Recomputing the rotation rule from the catalog, log and churn gives the same ranks.
The picked scopes are within the approval's scope and number.

verbs.title: Diff this run's findings against the last run
verbs.summary: Collect the picked scope's check outputs, list the checks that did not report, and sort every finding by fingerprint against the last run of the same scope: new, still open, fixed, gone unverified, gone unexplained, not checked or reopened.
verbs.outcome: A review run with its diff.

slots.name: check_outputs
slots.description: Pins of the outputs the scope's checks submitted.

slots.name: previous_run
slots.description: Pin of the last review run of the same scope, if any.

slots.name: findings
slots.description: Pins of the scope's findings, fixes and verifications on record.

steps: Use only the outputs of checks that ran on the scope's pinned version; list every other check under checks_not_run with its reason.

Sort every finding by the diff rules; a finding is fixed only with a recorded fix and a verification by a worker other than the fixer, and one a person closed as won't fix or duplicate goes under decided_seen with that decision.

Propose record-finding for new ones, propose-fix for still open ones without a proposal, verify-fix for unverified fixes, reproduce for unexplained ones, and triage and a stronger guard for reopened ones.
List every check whose version changed since the last run under checks_changed; its findings that are not seen again are not checked, never fixed or gone.
Set carried to the number of findings that are not new; a first run carries none.

acceptance.check: The run validates against template.review-run's schema.
The run passes every pinned loop check.
Sorting the pinned outputs and records by the diff rules gives the same lists.
counts equal the length of each diff list.

verbs.title: Append the run to the review log
verbs.summary: Append the review run to the review log by compare-and-set and recompute coverage: scopes reviewed within their intervals, never reviewed and overdue.
verbs.outcome: The next version of the review log.

slots.name: review_log
slots.description: Pin of the review log to update.

steps: Read the log's pinned version, append the run's entry and recompute coverage from the entries and the catalog.
Write the new version with the pinned version as the expected version; on a conflict, re-read and stop.
Never edit or remove an earlier entry.

acceptance.check: The log validates against template.review-log's schema.
Every entry of the pinned version is unchanged in the new one, and exactly one entry was added.
Coverage recomputes from the entries and the catalog.

verbs.title: Review your own change before handing it on
verbs.summary: Before handing a change on, map its paths to the scopes it touches, run those scopes' deterministic checks on it, record every problem found in your own work at once, and hand it to a different worker or a person.

slots.name: change
slots.description: Pin of the change: its commit or patch by digest.

steps: Map the change's paths to the catalog's scopes.
Run those scopes' deterministic checks on the change and list any that cannot run, with the reason.
Propose findings-to-fixes.record-finding for every problem found, including any fixed in the same change.
Name the different worker or person it goes to; never approve or verify your own change.

acceptance.check: The self-review validates against template.self-review's schema.
self_approval is false and handed_to names someone else.
Every failed check has a finding in own_findings.

network: Package installs inside the sandbox to run the scopes' checks on the change; no requests to any deployed system.

verbs.title: Read the log for what the loop misses
verbs.summary: Across a window of the review log, list scopes never reviewed or overdue twice, checks that never fail or often do not run, and findings that keep coming back, and propose a fix for each.

slots.name: review_runs
slots.description: Pins of the runs in the window.

steps: Count from the log's entries and the runs they pin only.
Propose checks-of-checks.validate-checks for a check that never fails, a finding for a check that often cannot run, and findings-to-fixes.review-patterns for a finding reopened again.
A change to the catalog or schedule goes back to a person through approve-schedule.

acceptance.check: The review validates against template.coverage-review's schema.
Every count recomputes from the pinned log and runs.
Each proposal addresses the gap it names.
